title: Fritz Von Erich: Exemplar
narrativeQuestion: What does a full credit America's Most Hated presentation look like?

chapters.title: Who and When
chapters.claim: Jack Adkisson of Jewett, Texas, wrestled as a German from Munich starting about 1953, eight years after a war that killed about 405,000 Americans.

chapters.title: How Wrestling Used the War
chapters.claim: The invented name, a fake brother, the Nazi salute and a 1953 letter show the German act was a business choice.

chapters.title: What Fritz Tells Us
chapters.claim: The Nazi act ended when Adkisson bought the Dallas office in 1966 and needed his hometown to cheer.

chapters.title: Does It Fit in Three Minutes?
chapters.claim: The script runs about two and a half minutes at 150 words a minute.

accuracyNotes: The 1953 letter quote comes from Notre Dame's Rare Books and Special Collections blog on the Jack Pfefer collection.
About 405,000 American military deaths follows the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs figure.
The Ringer describes Fritz's Nazi salute and Waldo's goose step.
